version.approval_notes:
This extension provides a virtual webcam for Firefox running inside proot Linux containers on Android (e.g. Tiny Computer), where the device camera cannot be accessed directly.

How it works:
- background.js fetches an MJPEG stream from 127.0.0.1 (default http://127.0.0.1:8765/video) and passes JPEG frames to the content scripts. The stream comes from camera-bridge/tcc_camera.py in the source repository, which reads the phone camera over ADB using scrcpy-server and ffmpeg, or from a camera app such as IP Webcam.
- main.js (MAIN world, all HTTPS pages) wraps navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia/enumerateDevices so pages see a camera named "Android Camera (Tiny Container)". Frames are drawn onto a canvas and exposed with canvas.captureStream(). It only acts when a page asks for video.
- isolated.js relays frames between the two.
- popup.html/popup.js: toolbar UI to connect/pair ADB and start/stop the camera.

Privacy: since the virtual camera bypasses Firefox's camera prompt, the extension shows its own prompt (prompt.html) the first time a site asks for video. background.js checks the decision for port.sender.url's origin before starting the camera or sending any frame, so a page cannot grant itself access; main.js only uses the answer to make getUserMedia fail with NotAllowedError. Decisions can be removed on the options page.

Permissions:
- Content scripts on all HTTPS sites: the virtual camera must be available to any video meeting or camera site the user opens, the same way a real webcam is.
- nativeMessaging: talks to the local host "tiny_container_camera" (camera-bridge/tcc_host.py, installed by camera-bridge/install.sh) to run adb connect/pair and to start/stop the camera bridge. Without the host the extension still works with an MJPEG app.
- Host permission for 127.0.0.1/localhost: to read the local stream. Other hosts are optional and requested on the options page.

No data leaves the device: the only network requests go to the local stream URL. No remote code, no analytics. The LOG_URL constant in background.js is empty in this build (it is only set in local debug builds).

Testing without a phone: run `python3 tools/mock_mjpeg.py --port 8765 any.jpg` from the source repository (https://github.com/CreatorB/tiny-container-camera), then open https://webcamtoy.com and choose the camera.

Source code is not minified or bundled. In the repository the code lives in extension/ and the manifest is merged from manifests/base.json + manifests/firefox.json by tools/build.py (`sh build.sh firefox`); the submitted package is dist/firefox/ as built, with no other transformation.

summary.en-US: Use your Android phone or tablet camera as a webcam in Firefox inside Tiny Computer / proot Linux, over ADB with no extra app. Works with Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Zoom and any other site.

description.en-US:
Running Linux on Android with Tiny Computer, Termux or another proot container is great for coding, until you need to join a video call with your team: Android does not let apps inside the container use the camera.

**Tiny Container Camera** fixes that. It reads the device camera over ADB (wireless debugging) and turns it into a webcam that every website can use.

**Features**

- Virtual camera named "Android Camera (Tiny Container)" on every HTTPS site: Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Zoom, Jitsi and others.
- No extra Android app: the camera is read over ADB with scrcpy's server, started and stopped automatically when a site needs it.
- Toolbar button to connect or pair ADB, pick the front or back camera, and start or stop it.
- Asks before a site can use the camera, like the browser does for a real webcam. Decisions are remembered per site.
- The device camera turns off by itself shortly after the last page stops using it.
- Works with any MJPEG stream too, such as the IP Webcam app.
- Your microphone keeps working as usual.
- No root, no kernel modules, no data collection.

**Quick start**

1. Turn on Wireless debugging on Android and connect ADB from the container.
2. Run `sh camera-bridge/install.sh` from the GitHub repository (once).
3. Install this add-on and click **Save and grant access** on the options page.
4. Pick **Android Camera (Tiny Container)** in your meeting settings.

**Video calls in proot**

On Android 11 and newer, WebRTC calls from a browser inside proot fail to connect because Android blocks netlink sockets. Run `sh webrtc-fix/install.sh` from the repository to fix it. The toolbar button shows whether the fix is active.

Full guide, troubleshooting and source code: [github.com/CreatorB/tiny-container-camera](https://github.com/CreatorB/tiny-container-camera)
